en: The Ritual Manual for the Recitation and Practice of the Five Secrets of Vajrasattva according to the Yoga of the *Vajraśekhara*, by [the author],
Grand Master of the Household (Kaifu Yitongsisi), Special Advancement (Teshen), Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial (Shi Hongluqing), and Duke of Sushan.

The Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery—honored with a purple robe, granted a fief of three thousand households, posthumously titled Minister of Works, and given the epithet "Great Mirror"—translated this by imperial decree, according to the Yoga of the Eighteen Assemblies of the *Vajraśekhara-sūtra* in One Hundred Thousand Verses.
It expounds the secret essentials of the internal merits of the Tathāgata’s sudden realization.
Now, as for those who practice the bodhisattva path and realize supreme enlightenment:
To bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings is the sublime path.
All sentient beings are submerged and wandering through the five destinies and the three realms;
if they do not enter the mandalas of the five families and the five secrets, [they cannot escape].
Without receiving the empowerment of the three secrets,
one’s own body of the three tainted karmas is able to deliver boundless sentient beings.
This is impossible.
Sentient beings of the five destinies are subsumed within the three realms, namely:
the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm.
The practice of the form and formless realms constitutes the path for transcending the three realms;
it takes the vows of individual liberation (*prātimokṣa*), meditative concentration (*samādhi*), and wisdom (*prajñā*) as its predominant conditions (*adhipatipratyaya*).
This is because those two upper realms are subsumed within the stages of meditative absorption (*dhyānabhūmi*).
In the desire realm there is no dhyāna; it is a stage of distracted goodness.
Even if one practices the rules for meditative concentration, one must still rely upon dhūta ascetic practices.
Relying on the seven stages of preparation,
because their faculties are weak and inferior,
even the fruit of an arhat or a pratyekabuddha is difficult to achieve for them.
How much more so for the great stage of Samantabhadra of the ten stages,
and the stage of Vairocana’s three bodies and universal radiance which is realized and established;
even though those of the two vehicles have realized the fruits of the path, [they cannot reach these].
One is unable to bring benefit and happiness to infinite sentient beings,
nor to those who practice the teachings of the Manifest (Exoteric) Vehicle.
After a long time, spanning three great incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*),
he then realizes unexcelled bodhi;
during that interval, there are nine retreats for every ten advances.
Or they may reach the seventh stage,
whereby they dedicate the merit and wisdom they have accumulated toward the fruits of the paths of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
Yet they are still unable to realize unsurpassed bodhi.
If one relies upon the Dharma of the internally realized, self-awakened noble wisdom as taught by the Svasaṃbhogakāya of Vairocana Buddha, [one may attain it].
Furthermore, through the wisdom of the Great Samantabhadra Vajrasattva’s *paranirmita-kāya*,
one encounters a maṇḍala ācārya in this very life and gains entry into the maṇḍala.
To fulfill the ritual action (*karmavācanā*),
he introduces Vajrasattva into his body by means of the Samantabhadra-samādhi.
By the power of this empowerment and majestic spiritual authority,
in a mere instant,
you shall realize immeasurable samayas and immeasurable dharani-gates.
By means of the inconceivable dharma,
one is able to transform the seeds of the innate grasping at a self and the grasping at phenomena within disciples;
thus, at that very moment, one gathers within the body the merit and wisdom accumulated over one great asaṃkhyeya kalpa.
Thus, one is born into the family of the Buddhas;
such a person is born from the mind of all Tathāgatas and is born from the mouth of the Buddha.
Born from the Buddha-dharma, born through transformation from the Dharma, one obtains the wealth of the Buddha-dharma;
"wealth of the Dharma" refers to the teachings on the three secrets and the bodhicitta. Merely by beholding the maṇḍala, [one attains this].
Because one gazes upon it with a heart of joy and pure faith for even a brief moment,
then, within the ālayavijñāna—
Having planted the seeds of the Vajradhātu and received the empowerment and the vajra-name of office,
from this point onward...
One receives the vast, profound, and inconceivable Dharma,
thereby transcending the two vehicles and the ten stages (*bhūmi*).
This is the dharma-gate of the five-secret yoga of the Great Vajrasattva.
During the four postures of walking, standing, sitting, and lying down,
one practices with uninterrupted mental attention toward all objects of seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing.
The two attachments to persons and phenomena are both entirely equal;
one realizes the first bhūmi in the present life and gradually ascends through the stages.
By practicing the Five Mysteries,
one remains unstained by and unattached to both nirvana and samsara,
even amidst the infinite cycle of birth and death within the five realms of existence.
Extensively performing acts of benefit and happiness,
he emanates ten billion bodies to roam among the various realms of existence, bringing sentient beings to spiritual accomplishment.
This causes one to realize the state of Vajrasattva.
The yogin, in a secluded mountain forest,
or in a consecrated chamber, or in whatever place he pleases, [should practice].
One should pay homage to the Tathāgatas of the four directions,
making offerings with one's body while reciting the root mantra;
this is because of the relinquishing of the body.
Then, one abandons the tainted substance of the three karmas and accomplishes the reception of the unimpeded discipline of the precepts throughout the three periods of time.
Next, one visualizes within the void the assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Then, placing the right knee upon the ground,
one should form the Vajrotthāna mudrā and recite its mantra,
while contemplating within the mind as follows:
I entreat all Tathāgatas not to remain attached to the blissful dwelling in the present life;
I pray only that you will have compassion for us, not transgressing your original vows,
and grant us your empowerment and protection.
One should confess and repent before the noble assembly, rejoice, and request [the turning of the wheel of Dharma]; furthermore, one should make five great vows.
Then, assume the Vajrasattva posture by placing the right foot over the left.
While forming the mudrā of meditative concentration, one should recite the mind of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. The mantra is:
Oṃ sarvayogacittotpādanaya mi. By reciting this mantra, [the vow is established].
All Tathāgatas cause the yogin to attain non-retrogression and the power to destroy all māras and adversaries;
such a person is equal to great bodhisattvas and all Tathāgatas.
The yogin reflects thus:
"I should generate the great heroic mind of Vajrasattva;
all sentient beings possess the nature of the Tathāgatagarbha."
Because Samantabhadra Bodhisattva pervades all sentient beings,
I shall cause all sentient beings to realize the state of Vajrasattva.
Furthermore, I reflect in this way:
All sentient beings possess the nature of the Vajra-treasury;
because they will inevitably obtain the vajra empowerment in the future,
I cause all sentient beings to swiftly attain the stage of the great bodhisattva empowerment.
He attained the stage of the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja and further reflected:
"All sentient beings possess the nature of the sublime Dharma-treasury."
Because it is able to transform all speech,
I shall cause all sentient beings to hear the entire collection of Mahāyāna sūtras and realize the stage of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Furthermore, he reflects in this way:
"The nature of the *karmadhātu* (repository of action) of all sentient beings is well capable of accomplishing all undertakings."
I shall cause all sentient beings to perform vast offerings at the abodes of all Tathāgatas,
so that they may realize the rank of the Bodhisattva Viśvakarman.
Furthermore, he reflects in this way:
"Since all sentient beings possess the fourfold nature of the treasury,
they shall attain the bodies of the four great bodhisattvas."
By the power of my merit, the power of the Tathāgata’s empowerment, and the power of the Dharma-realm, may all sentient beings swiftly realize the pure body of Vairocana. Recite the mantra:
Oṃ sarvatathāgata-saṃstuta-sarvajñatā-pratīccha tathāgatādhiṣṭhāna. Immediately form the vajra-joined-palms mudrā (*vajra-añjali-mudrā*).
Join the two palms with the fingers interlaced, the right hand pressing over the left, and recite the mantra:
*Oṃ vajra-lanjali*. By forming this mudrā, [the following occurs].
The ten pāramitās are perfected,
and the two accumulations of merit and wisdom are accomplished.
Next, bind the vajra-bond mudrā.
Perform the preceding vajra-joined palms (*vajra-añjali*), then interlace the outer hands to form fists and recite the mantra:
*Oṃ vajramuṣṭi*. By forming this seal, one immediately accomplishes the wisdom of Vajra-liberation (*vajra-vimukti-jñāna*).
Next, form the Vajrabandha mudrā.
Strike one’s own heart three times while reciting the mantra:
Oṃ vajrarājamudra traṭ. By forming this seal, [the empowerment is attained].
Being able to destroy the ten kinds of afflictions that shroud and obscure body and mind,
one then summons all mudrās,
which abide within body and mind.
The practitioner who acts in accordance with this accomplishes all tasks.
As for "all seals," they are the Great Wisdom Seal, the Samaya Wisdom Seal, the Dharma Wisdom Seal, and the Karma Wisdom Seal.
Next, form the Vajrāveśa mudrā.
With both hands in the vajra-bind,
bend the thumbs and middle fingers and place them respectively within the space of the ring fingers, while reciting the mantra:
Oṃ vajrāveśaya. By forming this mudrā, the four wisdom-mudrās are manifested;
it possesses great power and brings swift accomplishment.
Next, bind the Vajramuṣṭi-samaya-mudrā.
Following the previous mudrā, bend the forefinger (tarjanī) to press against the back of the middle finger (madhyamā) and the ring finger (anāmikā), and recite the mantra:
Oṃ vajramuṣṭi vaṃ. By binding this mudrā, [the vow is established].
The "All-Seals" that are capable of binding firmly refers to the four seals; they shall never be lost from within the body and mind of the practitioner.
Next, one binds the Samaya-seal.
Form the double vajra-bind with both hands.
Join the two middle fingers upright and place them at the heart while reciting the mantra:
*Oṃ vajrabandha saṃsthāpaya svāhā*. Having recited the mantra, perform the mudrā.
Visualize a moon disc behind you as a halo,
with your body situated within it;
imagine yourself as Vajrasattva.
By binding this mudrā and reciting this mantra, all mudrās bound within all families,
such as the Great Wisdom Mudrā, as well as all the Vajra Mudrās of the body,
speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, [are accomplished].
One's merit shall not be wasted, and one shall not dare to transgress.
If one recites it one thousand times,
all mudrās will be accomplished.
Next, bind the Great Samaya Reality Seal (Mahāsamayatatvamudrā).
Form the vajra-bond with both hands;
insert the ring fingers into the palms so that they interlace.
The aspects of generosity-wisdom and meditative concentration-wisdom are joined together like a single-pronged vajra.
With the fingers of the *kṣānti* (patience) and *praṇidhāna* (vow) mudrās touching the heart, recite the mantra as follows:

Recite: *Oṃ vajrasattva samayam anupālaya vajrasattvatvenopatiṣṭha dṛḍho me bhava sutoṣyo me bhava supoṣyo me bhava anurakto me bhava sarvasiddhiṃ me prayaccha sarvakarmasu ca me cittaṃ śreyaḥ kuru hūṃ ha ha ha ha hoḥ bhagavan sarvatathāgatavajra mā me muñca vajrībhava mahāsamayasattva āḥ*.
By binding this mudrā and touching the heart with it, Vajrasattva enters pervasively into the body and mind.
Grant swift accomplishment;
may all aspirations and desires be fulfilled.
Next, bind the Great Wisdom Seal of Vajrasattva.
Then, release the preceding mudrā.
Form vajra-fists with both hands;
place the left hand at the hip.
With the right hand, assume the posture of brandishing and casting the vajra,
placing it at the heart.
With the right foot pressing down upon the left, recite the mantra as follows:
Having recited *vajrasattvaṃ haṃ*, visualize yourself as Vajrasattva,
seated upon a great lotus flower within a great moon disc.
He wears a jeweled crown of the five Buddhas;
his countenance is serene and joyful, and his body is like the color of the moon,
transparent and luminous both within and without.
Arousing great compassion, they deliver the inexhaustible and boundless realms of sentient beings,
causing them to attain the body of Vajrasattva,
with the three secrets operating in unison, their measure equal to space.
Because of being in union with the great wisdom-mudrā of yoga,
even if one were to transgress the Dharma,
commit grave offenses, and create various obstacles, [the result would be as follows].
Because they hold that Great Wisdom Seal,
they are honored, revered, and respected by all Tathāgatas.
Should anyone prostrate to them, make offerings to them, honor them, or praise them, [they likewise receive such merit].
Then one sees all the Tathāgatas and Vajrasattva.
One should abide in this Great Wisdom Seal (mahājñānamudrā),
and visualize the wisdom-body of Vajrasattva before oneself as being identical to one's own body.
Visualize them surrounded by the four seals,
all within a single moon disc and a single lotus,
each abiding in their original posture and holding their respective insignia.
Each wears a precious crown of the five Buddhas.
The yogin focuses intently on Vajrasattva before him;
with an undistracted mind, he recites the mantra as follows:
By reciting this mantra, *vajrasattva āveśaya*,
Vajrasattva shall manifest as an *āveśa*.
Next, recite the mantra:
By reciting this mantra, *vajrasattva dṛśya*,
one causes Vajrasattva to appear within meditative concentration.
With complete clarity, one recites the four-syllable vidyā-mantra:
*Jraḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ*. By reciting this mantra, [the result is attained].
The wisdom-body of Vajrasattva causes [the practitioner] to summon, enter, bind, and delight,
merging into a single essence with the meditative body of the yogin.
Next, form the surata mudrā:
with both hands in the vajra-bond,
insert the right thumb into the mouth of the left "tiger" (the little finger).
Then, one performs the empowerment upon the four locations—the heart, forehead, throat, and crown—reciting the mantra once for each: *sūtradhāraḥ svāhā*.
By means of this empowerment through the mudrā, [the effect is achieved].
The four pāramitās each abide in their original positions,
constantly and eternally providing protection and support.
Next, one forms the seal of the Five-Buddha Jewel-Crown.
Form the double-vajra-bind (*vajrabandha*) with both hands;
join the thumbs and ring fingers together, erect and parallel,
and bend their upper joints into the shape of a sword.
With the *vīrya* (effort) mudrā attached to the *kṣānti* (patience) mudrā on the back,
place the seal upon the crown of the head;
next, place it at the hairline, and then place it on the right side of the crown.
Next, place it behind the crown, and next place it on the left side of the crown.
Recite the mantra once for each. The mantra is:
Oṃ sarvatathāgata-ratnābhiṣeka-āveśaya huṃ jjaḥ. By forming this mudrā, [the empowerment is bestowed].
One attains the stage of the consecration of Vajrasattva of all Tathāgatas.
Next, one binds the Vajramālā mudrā:
with both hands, form the vajra-fists.
The two hands are entwined and bound in front of the forehead,
separated at the sides,
and again bound behind the head.
Then, from the *Dānabuddhi*, one should slowly open [the eyes] like the silk streamers of a hanging crown. Reciting the mantra:
OṂ VAJRAMĀLĀBHIṢEKAM VAṂ, one should then form the Armor Seal (*kavaca-mudrā*).
Don armor over the entire body.
Next, form the mudrā of joy.
With both hands palms flat, clap them together to bring forth joy, and recite the mantra as follows:
VAJRA-DṚŚYE HŪṂ. Next, bind the Great Wisdom Seal (Mahājñānamudrā) of the aforementioned Vajrasattva and recite the root mantra:
OṂ MAHĀ-SUKHA-VAJRASATTVA JAH HŪṂ VAṂ HOḤ VAṂ HOḤ SUKHA-STHASIDDHI VAṂ. Next, one should bind the four secret Karma seals.
Then, recite the Vajra Song of Praise.
For each four-line stanza of this praise, bind one mudrā.
As you recite each line, chant the praise as follows:
*Sarva-nirāka-satkarmaṇaḥ siddhaṃ vajrasattvapramokṣaṇaṃ bhavatu me mahāsukha-nirvṛti-śāntaye pratisiddhārthaprāptaye.* (4) Next, perform the Vajra-cupid mudrā.
Form two vajra-fists;
visualize the left fist holding a bow,
while the right fist holds an arrow in the posture of shooting.
One immediately becomes this Honored One.
To seal the body, recite the mantra:
*sarvanirarga-sukha-sattvānām*. Then, bind the *kṛtikara* mudrā.
Seal it as before.
Crossing the two fists and embracing them at the chest,
one immediately becomes this deity.
Sealing the body, recite the mantra:
*sattvaṃ vajrasattvābhyoḥ prasīda*. Next, form the seal of Vajrarāga.
Following the previous two vajra-fists,
support the left fist under the right elbow and extend the right arm upward in the manner of a banner.
One immediately becomes this deity.
Forming the seal upon the body, recite the mantra:
*sarvavid mahā-sūkṣma-nirhāra-jñāna-krodha*. Next, bind the Vajragarva-mudrā.
Place the two vajra-fists at the navel;
incline the head slightly to the left in the manner of prostration,
and one immediately becomes this deity.
Sealing the body, recite the mantra:
*pratiṣṭhā-siddhy-ājñā-garbha-nātha*. Next, form the fivefold secret samaya-mudrā.
Then, one should form the Vajrasattva Samaya-mudrā:
perform the vajra-bind,
bend the ring fingers and thumbs so that they enter and join within the palms as before.
Meditative concentration and wisdom, as well as generosity and insight,
support one another like a single-pronged vajra.
Recite the mantra as follows:
By forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra *sūratasatvaṃ*,
one’s supernormal powers, lifespan, majestic power,
and marks of excellence become equal to those of Vajrasattva.
Next, bind the Vajra-Samaya Mudrā of Desire.
Following the previous mudrā, bend the upper joints of the index fingers so that their nails meet at their backs.
Pressing both the meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) and wisdom (*prajñā*) upon it, recite the mantra:
*Jrīṃ jvala jvala dṛṣṭiśāyakīmata*. By forming this mudrā, [the result is attained].
One is able to sever the subtle afflictions of the ground of ignorance (*avidyāvāsabhūmi*).
Then, form the *Kilikīla-samaya-mudrā* as before,
with the right wisdom finger pressing against the left dhyāna finger, crossing them at the joints, and recite the mantra as follows:
HŪṂ VAJRA KĪLI KĪLAYA HŪṂ. By binding this mudrā, one is able to rescue and protect the entire realm of sentient beings who are suffering.
All shall attain the samādhi of great peace and bliss.
Next, bind the Vajra-Love Samaya-mudrā:
following the previous mudrā, interlace the *vajra-śakti* fingers with one another, while the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhāna* fingers remain as before.
The powers of progress and effort are joined together like the shape of an eye;
the square marks of the precepts are joined vertically;
generosity and wisdom are likewise. Recite the mantra as follows:
By reciting "VAṂ VAJRAJVALINI SAMĀRAKṢA" while forming this mudrā,
one attains the liberation of great compassion and comes to cherish all sentient beings as if they were an only child.
One should give rise to a mind that seeks to rescue, protect, and bring peace and happiness to all.
Next, bind the Vajra Pride Samaya Mudrā.
Following the previous procedure, touch the two thighs—first the right, then the left—and recite the mantra as follows:
By forming this mudrā while reciting *khavajrakāmīṣvarī-tvaṃ*,
one attains the perfection of great vigor (*mahāvīryapāramitā*).
In a single instant, one is able to perform vast offerings before all Tathāgatas in infinite worlds;
thereafter, one abides in the Vajrasattva-samaya.
The mantra for the hundred-syllable Vajrasattva, which is the realization-mantra of the Mahāyāna,
is as follows: Oṃ vajrasattva samayam anupālaya vajrasattvatvenopatiṣṭha.
Oṃ nṛtyaiva bhava sudṛśyaiva bhavānugataiva bhava supuṣyaiva bhava sarvasiddhiṃ pratyakṣaṃ kuru sarvakāmasaukhyam cittasiri... [dvitīya] |||1||
HAYAGRĪVA HŪṂ HA HA HA HA HOḤ PRAJÑĀPĀRAMITĀ VAJRAMĀMEÑCA VĀRĪBHAVA MAHASAMAYA SATTVĀḤ ĀḤ.
Immediately, he enters the vajrasattva-samādhi.
Then, bind the Great Wisdom Seal (Mahājñānamudrā) and recite the Mahāyāna Vajrasattva Sādhana-mantra, saying:
*Vajrasattva*. Alternatively, remain abiding in the Great Wisdom Seal.
Or, holding a rosary, one may recite the mantra without limit,
provided that one does not become exhausted;
for by remaining in samādhi while reciting this mantra, [the goal is achieved].
In this very life, one realizes immeasurable samādhis and is able to manifest the body of the tutelary deity;
all Tathāgatas appear before one.
Having realized the five supernormal powers,
they travel through all worlds in the ten directions,
extensively performing boundless deeds for the benefit, peace, and happiness of sentient beings.
Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining,
the yogin is always surrounded by his four retinues,
dwelling upon a great lotus flower within a single lunar disc.
Vajrasattva is Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
he is the eldest son of all Tathāgatas and the bodhicitta of all Tathāgatas.
He is the ancestral teacher of all Tathāgatas;
therefore, all Tathāgatas pay homage to Vajrasattva.
As it is said in the sūtra:
"The samādhi of Vajrasattva is called the Dharma of all Buddhas;
this dharma can accomplish the path of all Buddhas, for apart from this, there is no Buddha."
The Vajra of Desire is named Prajñāpāramitā;
it is that which can penetrate all Buddha-dharmas.
Unimpeded and unobstructed like a vajra, it is able to give birth to all Buddhas.
The Vajrakīlikīla is the samādhi of Ākāśagarbha.
May they grant peace and happiness to infinite sentient beings;
may they rescue and deliver infinite sentient beings who are submerged in the mud of poverty and deprivation;
and may they cause all their desired aspirations, both mundane and supramundane, to be fully realized.
The one who loves Vajra is the Bodhisattva Tārā,
who abides in the liberation of great compassion.
Compassionately mindful of infinite sentient beings undergoing suffering,
he constantly cherishes the intent to deliver them and bestow peace and happiness.
This is the Vajra Pride.
This is the perfection of great diligence.
Abiding in unimpeded liberation,
one extensively performs the Buddha-work for infinite Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, for the sake of benefiting sentient beings,
one who holds the vajra of desire takes up the vajra bow and arrow and shoots all contaminated seeds within the ālayavijñāna.
This constitutes the attainment of the Great Perfect Mirror Wisdom (*ādarśa-jñāna*).
As for "Vajra-Ketukīla embracing Vajrasattva," this symbolizes the purification of the deluded attachments of the seventh consciousness toward the eighth consciousness.
Through the transformation of self-delusion, the view of self, self-pride, and self-love,
the Wisdom of Equality is perfected;
this is Vajrasattva abiding in the Great Wisdom Seal (Mahājñānamudrā).
From Vajradhātu to Vajraghaṇṭābodhisattva,
they manifest the bodies of the fruit-virtues of self-enjoyment and other-enjoyment through the thirty-seven wisdoms.
Those who cherish Vajra hold the makara banner.

The ability to purify the mental consciousness (*manovijñāna*) so that it takes as its object both pure and defiled contaminated minds constitutes the Wisdom of Wondrous Observation (*pratyavekṣaṇājñāna*).
As for "Vajra Pride":
Place the two vajra-fists at the navel to symbolize the purification of the five consciousnesses and the physical body of obstructive matter;
then arouse great diligence and valor.
He causes all sentient beings, without exception,
to attain Buddhahood instantaneously;
he is able to purify the five bodies of sensory consciousness and transform them into the Wisdom of Accomplishing What Is Done (*kṛtyānuṣṭhāna-jñāna*).
The Desire-Vajra is the eye of wisdom;
it observes the dependent nature (*paratantra-svabhāva*) in its stained and pure aspects,
knowing that all phenomena are neither existent nor non-existent.
Vajrakīrti observes the pure aspect of the dependent nature with undefiled wisdom.
In the state of the fruition of virtue, it is neither identical to nor different from the perfected nature (*pariniṣpanna-svabhāva*).
One knows that all phenomena are neither identical to nor different from bodhi and nirvāṇa.
As for Vajrasattva:
This is the svabhāvakāya.
Being neither born nor extinguished, its measure is equal to empty space;
it is thus the body that pervades the entire dharmadhātu.
The Vajra-Lover,
with the divine eye of great compassion,
beholds within the bodies of all sentient beings the essence of Samantabhadra, neither increasing nor decreasing.
As for the Vajra-pride:
with the pure and unobstructed fleshly eye,
one observes all sentient beings abiding in the stage of ordinary worldlings (*pṛthagjana*).
Although the inherent nature is pure even when obscured by afflictions,
if one accords with great diligence,
one immediately attains stainless purity.
Vajrasattva is the body of Vairocana Buddha;
Kāmadhātu-vajra is the Vajra-pāramitā;
Kīlikīla is the Ratna-pāramitā.
Vajrarāga is the dharma-pāramitā;
Vajramāna is the karma-pāramitā;
and Vajrasattva is that very Bhagavān Akṣobhya Tathāgata.
The Desire-Vajra is Vajrasattva;
Kīlikīla is the Vajra King;
the Love-Vajra is Vajrarāga.
Vajragarva is Vajrasādhu;
Vajrasattva is that Blessed One, Ratnasaṃbhava Tathāgata.
Rāgavajra is the Vajraratna; Kīlikīla is the Vajrasūrya;
and Rativajra is the Vajraketu.
Vajra-pride is Vajra-laughter.
Vajrasattva is that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja.
Desire-vajra is Vajradharma.

To cause the realization of non-defiled wisdom,
one takes the makara-banner of the vajra of craving as the great compassion vajra-chain.
Abiding in birth and death for immeasurable kalpas,
their minds remain unshakable;
they take the liberation of all sentient beings as their path.
As for the Vajra-Pride,
one takes great diligence as the Prajñā-vajra-bell to awaken those sentient beings who dwell in the cave-dwelling of ignorance and whose latent tendencies remain dormant.
The Samantabhadra maṇḍala does not depart from the five bodies (pañcakāya).

The five secrets of Vajrasattva constitute the Tathāgatakula;

The meaning of the liberation of great compassion;
the single lunar disc with its circular radiance signifies the meaning of great wisdom.
Therefore, by virtue of great wisdom,
the bodhisattva is not defiled by saṃsāra;
by virtue of great compassion, he does not abide in nirvāṇa.
As stated in the sūtras,
there are three kinds of beings (sattva):
namely, the ignorant being, the wise being, and the vajra-being.
By means of Vajrasattva, one distinguishes him from the other two types of sattvas;
a practitioner who has attained this Vajrayāna is then called Vajrasattva.
Therefore, the Bodhisattva of supreme wisdom constantly acts for the benefit of sentient beings until the very end of saṃsāra.
Yet they do not proceed toward nirvāṇa.
By what dharma can such a state be attained?
Therefore, it is through both prajñā and upāya.
Sustained by the power of Prajñāpāramitā,
all phenomena and all modes of existence are entirely pure.
The two types of grasping— grasping at phenomena (*dharma*) and grasping at persons (*pudgala*)— are what constitute all things and all that is named.
Therefore, [the Buddha] desires to discipline the world through [the teachings on] desire and so forth,
in order to bring about their complete purification.
Having subdued those in the Peak of Existence and the evil destinies,
he has exhausted all states of being by dwelling in the *ākāśagarbha-samādhi*.
Regarding the two attachments to persons and phenomena,
one realizes that they are all equal and pure, just like a lotus; therefore,
it is said that the nature of the lotus is pure.
That which is inherently pure is not defiled by impurities;
the nature of all desires is likewise so.
It is undefiled, yet it benefits sentient beings—this is what it means to benefit sentient beings.
Bringing about peace, happiness, and benefit,
one dwells in the state of Great Sovereignty;
therefore, the Great Desire attains purification.
Great peace, bliss, and abundance;
attaining mastery over the three realms;
able to bring about firm benefit—O you who bring about firm benefit!
The bodhicitta is the cause.
There are two kinds of causes:
saving boundless sentient beings is the cause.
Unsurpassed bodhi is the fruit.
Furthermore, great compassion is the root;
one should likewise abide in a mind of great compassion.
It cannot be shaken by the winds of the realms of the two vehicles;
this is entirely due to the Great Expedient Means (*mahopāya*).
As for the Great Expedient Means, the three secrets (*triguhyaka*) of the Vajra serve as the predominant condition (*adhipatipratyaya*).
